4/🧵 On 13 TWIN tasks, BiCICLe reaches 70.5% average success, +6.1 points over the best training-free baseline, and outperforms most supervised methods.

We also transfer it to 3 real-world tasks without hardware-specific retraining.

tweets.body:
3/🧵 BiCICLe treats bimanual control as a multi-agent problem. A leader predicts the action for one arm. A follower predicts the other arm conditioned on that action.

One difficult joint prediction becomes two coordinated single-arm predictions. https://t.co/6Ju5WeqZzL

tweets.body:
2/🧵 In-context learning is appealing for robotics: no fine-tuning, just a few demonstrations in context.

But bimanual manipulation makes this much harder: the action space is larger, the arms are tightly coupled, and context gets expensive fast.

tweets.body: In this work, we explore how agents can anticipate the consequences of their actions before executing them. Instead of relying on slow visual simulation, we introduce DILLO, a distilled language-action world model for fast, proactive agent steering.
